lines.text: At an hour and twenty-four minutes, you're in orbit, standing still.
lines.phonemes: æɾ ɐn ˈaʊɚ ænd twˈɛntifˈɔːɹ mˈɪnɪts, jʊɹ ɪn ˈɔːɹbɪt, stˈændɪŋ stˈɪl.

lines.text: At a day of about an hour and twenty-four minutes, the ground under you moves at seven point nine kilometers a second. That is the speed of a satellite in a low orbit. At that speed, the push outward exactly cancels gravity. You weigh nothing. You are no longer standing on the Earth. You are orbiting it, one stride above the surface, with the whole equator going by beneath you.

lines.text: And past that point, the equator can no longer keep its own rock. This is as far as a simple sum can honestly take us.
